central_topic: Coverage and common-simplex-volume efficiency of externally split-calibrated, training-adaptive ILR ellipsoids for strictly positive continuous compositional regression across synthetic noise, boundary, and covariate-shift regimes.
core_methods: Independent split-conformal calibration at nominal joint coverage 0.90
Isometric log-ratio (ILR) representation with quadratic-feature ridge location and log-residual variance regression
Deterministic four-fold out-of-fold location residuals with an all-training-row final location refit
Training-fixed predicted-boundary tertiles with pooled and group-shrunk residual second-moment shapes
Positive-definite, input-adaptive ILR ellipsoids returned through Cholesky factors
comparators: Evaluated: Euclidean residual balls intersected with the simplex, using clipped and renormalized composition-space ridge predictions
Evaluated: isotropic ILR residual balls, equivalent to Aitchison-distance regions
Evaluated variants: single 75/25 location/residual split versus four-fold residual fitting; hard boundary-tertile routing versus continuous convex covariance interpolation
Sanity controls, not learned baselines: point-copy singleton, full simplex, constant inputs, and training-pair derangement
Literature-only positioning: conditional versus marginal coverage and weighted conformal inference under covariate shift; neither groupwise calibration nor importance weighting was implemented
benchmarks: Local synthetic C1: K=3 homoskedastic logistic-normal regression with five Gaussian covariates
Local synthetic C2: K=3 covariate-dependent heteroskedastic logistic-normal regression
Local synthetic C3: K=8 near-boundary Dirichlet regression with strictly positive responses
Local synthetic C4: K=8 Dirichlet regression with test-only covariate location and scale shift
Matched C2-derived controls: C5 constant covariates and C6 deranged training covariate-response pairing; these are not independent datasets
architectural_shifts: Representation comparison: direct simplex-coordinate Euclidean balls versus isotropic ILR balls versus covariate-adaptive ILR ellipsoids; all use small quadratic-feature ridge predictors, not neural architectures

Residual-estimation change: one 75/25 training split replaced by four-fold out-of-fold residuals and a full-training location refit; training-only changes do not replace independent conformal calibration

Shape-routing change: hard training-frozen boundary tertiles versus continuous convex interpolation of training-estimated positive-definite covariance shapes; search evidence does not establish a reliable interpolation advantage
result_driven_themes: The four-fold residual variant has the highest recorded search utility; its comparison with the split variant also changes location training size and is not a mechanism-isolating ablation

Final paired seed evidence favors adaptive ILR ellipsoids over isotropic ILR balls in both coverage and volume, but the Euclidean baseline has smaller average volume and no resolved coverage difference

Regime dependence matters: near-boundary C3 regions occupy nearly the full simplex, while shifted C4 coverage is below the nominal target; no universal efficiency or shift-robustness claim is supported

Marginal coverage and descriptive covariate-stratum coverage differ; the recorded zero worst-stratum summary includes empty strata under constant-input controls and is not evidence of observed zero coverage in a populated group

Efficiency must be compared using shared uniform-simplex probes, not raw volumes in different coordinate systems; Wilson intervals, paired seed bootstrap intervals, and integration errors address different uncertainty sources, with only three search and five final seeds

queries.rationale: Starter-listed foundation for independent split calibration, finite-sample rank selection, and marginal rather than conditional guarantees; the run uses an externally calibrated 0.90 joint-coverage threshold. This is a known-title lookup, not a search for the prohibited task-specific paper.

queries.query: isometric log-ratio transformation Aitchison distance compositional data
queries.rationale: Grounds the actual ILR representation and isotropic log-ratio baseline against Euclidean simplex geometry. The starter-listed Aitchison background is relevant; no Hellinger geometry or exact-zero extension was evaluated. Keep this representation-only query separate from conformal terminology.

queries.query: multivariate split conformal prediction Mahalanobis ellipsoidal regions
queries.rationale: Positions the implemented vector-valued standardized residual norm and Cholesky-shaped prediction regions against general multivariate conformal regression, without searching the prohibited composition-specific evaluation topic.

queries.query: out-of-fold residuals heteroskedastic regression variance estimation
queries.rationale: Targets the highest-utility search variant's four-fold residual construction and all-row variance fit. Relevant work should distinguish training-only residual estimation from CV+, jackknife+, and cross-conformal calibration, which were not implemented. The simultaneous location refit prevents isolated causal attribution.

queries.query: covariance shrinkage positive definite heteroskedastic multivariate regression
queries.rationale: Grounds the pooled/group residual second-moment shrinkage and stable positive-definite shapes shared by the strongest variants. Continuous covariance interpolation is a secondary evaluated variation, not an established improvement or a new neural architecture.

queries.query: logistic-normal Dirichlet regression compositional responses boundary
queries.rationale: The actual benchmark consists only of local positive-composition logistic-normal and Dirichlet generators with K=3 or K=8. These model families clarify heteroskedasticity and near-boundary behavior more precisely than local case IDs or unused public dataset names. Do not add conformal terminology to this query.

queries.query: distribution-free predictive inference marginal conditional coverage limitations
queries.rationale: Explains why one pooled conformal threshold and input-adaptive shapes do not provide subgroup guarantees. The released sign-stratum diagnostics are descriptive, and empty control strata must not be interpreted as populated groups with zero coverage.

Starter-listed comparator literature for the explicit test-only covariate shift in C4 and its below-target observed coverage. Weighted conformal inference is a related-work alternative, not an evaluated baseline or a guarantee enjoyed by the unweighted method.

queries.query: multivariate prediction regions volume efficiency Monte Carlo integration
queries.rationale: Grounds evaluation by common-measure region volume rather than incomparable coordinate-space volumes. Shared uniform-simplex probes yield paired Monte Carlo errors, distinct from finite-test coverage intervals and seed uncertainty; near-full-simplex C3 volumes make efficiency limitations scientifically relevant.
